title: The Kid and the Wolf

full_text:
A little kid goat stood upon the high thatched roof of a sheepcote, looking down at a wolf passing by the fence below. Feeling completely secure behind the high walls, the little goat began shouting insults, sticking out his tongue, and mocking the predator's gray fur and wicked eyes.

The wolf paused, looked up calmly at the insolent little creature, and replied:

"Taunt on, little fool! It is not you who reviles me, but the sturdy roof and high wall upon which you stand! Take away the stone beneath your hooves, and we would see how brave your tongue would be!"
moral: Cowardly taunts from a place of safety show no real valor; it is the wall that speaks.
